rows.Incident Description:
Room Guest 2014, Ms. Sterling, visited The Verandah for breakfast with her family, a total of eight persons. During service, the guest raised a comment regarding the chef’s attitude at the egg station. Upon being informed, Manager immediately offered a sincere apology and attempted to follow up by arranging a replacement order. However, the guest declined further action and stated that she only wished to bring the matter to our attention.

Finding
Guest mentioned to the chef that she would like her egg preparation changed from sunny side up to well done. Chef recalled that the guest had visited the previous day and had ordered sunny side up, and therefore assumed he might have misheard the request. As a result, the order was not amended accordingly, which led to the guest’s dissatisfaction.

Action
A briefing will be conducted with the culinary team to reinforce that the guest’s request at the time of ordering must always take priority, regardless of previous visits or past preferences.
rows.Subject: Verandah | Mr. Daniel Sterling | Guest Comment - F&B

rows.Incident Description:
Incident:
At 7:15 PM during checkout, Mr. Okada expressed dissatisfaction regarding their spa experience. He approached the reception to discuss his wife’s concerns. While Mr. Okada was speaking with the spa reception, Mrs. Okada also approached and shared her complaints about her therapist.
Guest Complaints
1.	Mrs. Okada commented that the therapist was not using Margy’s products, based on her knowledge and previous experience at Pen Tokyo.
2.	She doubted the products were Margy’s because she observed the therapist mixing several products.
3.	She disliked the therapist’s attitude when explaining the treatment price and the difference between Margy’s and VOYA.
4.	She felt the therapist was not accommodating to her requests.
While the spa reception was trying to explain the treatment procedure and product preparation, Mr. Okada interrupted, stating they were unhappy with their experience and had spent a lot. Guest Relations expressed sincere apologies and assured them that the incident would be investigated. Mr. Okada mentioned he was satisfied with his own treatment but stated that Mrs. Okada would not return. Both guests left unhappy.
 
Findings
•	Both guests were booked for Peninsula Time, and Guest Relations informed them about the VOYA products 
•	The therapist confirmed that Margy’s products were used as approved by the Spa Director.

Action Plan
-Guest Relations will follow up via email. The communication will focus on corrective
-Spa will investigate further of what happened during the treatment.

rows.Incident Description:
During the wedding dinner event, video playback experienced blackout due to unstable connection. Immediate technical adjustment was applied; however, during the second playback, the video blacked out 4 times within a four minute duration.
RM approached the host extend a sincere apology and to explain the situation. With the host’s approval, a test playback was conducted together with EDS without audio, while service was ongoing. The video played smoothly during the third playback.
Subsequently, a second video requested by the host was played and completed without any interruption. The host acknowledged that this was an isolated incident and expressed appreciation for the follow up and handling of the matter.
As a gesture of goodwill, the setup fee of $ 8,000net was waived.
Findings:
The AV setup was completed in the afternoon, followed by two successful test runs:
1.	Initial test after full setup completion
2.	Final test after touched up(cover for the wire) and cleaning done.
EDS technician was unable to identify the root cause of the blackout. As playback resumed smoothly afterward, it was recommended that no further adjustments be made.

rows.Incident Description:
At 5:19 PM, B&T Supervisor informed DM that a guest had reported damage to her silver suitcase, claiming that one wheel found missing and accusing the B&T team of causing the damage. B&T team advised that they would review the matter and have DM follow up with the guest.
 Duty Manager immediately reviewed the CCTV footage and confirmed that the guest’s suitcase already had only three wheels upon arrival at the hotel at 4:18 PM. The footage showed the guest arriving via a self-arranged MPV (plate:YS6151). Attempts were made to contact the guest by phone to provide an update; however, all calls went unanswered, and a message was left in the guest’s room.

At 11:30 PM, the guest returned to the hotel and requested to meet with DM. During the conversation, DM explained the CCTV findings. The guest requested to view the footage, but request was politely declined. The guest then asked for a resolution, and DM offered to either assist in arranging suitcase repairs or purchase a replacement on behalf of the guest. The guest declined to bear any charges and instead requested compensation from the hotel. DM reiterated the CCTV findings and explained that compensation could not be offered under the circumstances.

Following this, the guest stated she wished to “forget about the suitcase” but requested a complimentary room upgrade due to the overall experience, where DM declined this request as well. The guest subsequently stated she would seek police assistance and DM assured her that the hotel would fully cooperate should the police conduct an investigation.

rows.Incident Description:
The Front Desk team reported (2710) Mr Gora’s complaints concerning the spa reception yesterday, 17 January 2026 (evening).
1.	He went to the spa to make a reservation and was informed by the spa reception that she would check availability and call him back. However, he did not receive any follow up call.
2.	He stated that he purchased the products, and upon opening the box, the item inside was incorrect. He further expressed the belief that the spa reception is dishonest.
3.	The Front Desk agent ask us to void the product
 
Findings:
Reservation:
1.	At around 8:30 PM, the guest walked in and made reservations for body massage sessions on 18th, 24th, and 25th January at 12:00 PM, with a duration of 60 minutes each.
2.	The spa reception informed the guest that there was no availability tomorrow (18 January) and offered to call him back once the reservation could be arranged. The guest advised that he would not be in his room as he would be having dinner at Imasa. He requested the spa reception to contact Imasa to inform them that he would be late for his reservation. The spa reception assisted as instructed.
3.	A confirmation card was subsequently sent by the spa reception to provide the guest with the booking details, including the future booking on 24 and 25 January
 
Product purchase:
1.  Upon presentation of the product by the spa reception, the guest expressed concern that it appeared to be a different package.
2.  The spa receptionist explained that it was the same product and that only the packaging had been updated.
3.  Despite the explanation, the guest remained uncertain and decided to cancel the purchase.
 
At 6:25 PM (18 Jan), The Spa Supervisor extended a sincere apology for the earlier inconvenience and offered the guest a complimentary 15-minute extension as a gesture of goodwill. The guest expressed appreciation and mentioned that, in future, he would prefer to be informed in advance to avoid any misunderstanding. The guest confirmed his bookings on 24th and 25th January at 1:00 PM for a 60-minute body massage on each day.

rows.Incident Description:
Mr. Kelvin Lau visited the hotel in person today to share feedback regarding his buffet dining experience on the evening of 23 January. He stated that his visit today was purely to provide feedback.

Findings
Mr. Lau felt that the overall food quality had declined compared to previous visits. Some dishes did not meet his expectations, possibly due to the food temperature not being sufficiently hot. The variety of food items was not to his preference. On that evening, he was seated in a PDR, which was relatively far from the buffet counters. As a result, the area had less guest traffic, and he felt there was less attention and engagement.

Action
AM apology was extended to Mr. Lau for his unsatisfactory experience. Appreciation was expressed for his valuable feedback and business card was provided for future contact. He was informed that the culinary team would closely monitor food temperature and variety. It was also noted that for future reservations, seating arrangements would be made closer to the buffet counters whenever possible.

rows.Incident Description:
At 5:00 p.m., the Assistant Director of Housekeeping reported that a guest had raised concerns regarding their down jacket after laundry service. The guest observed scratches on the Moncler jacket's fabric and noted that a smoke odor remained even after washing. HSKP extended their apologies and explained that the garment had been cleaned according to the care instructions attached to the item. However, the guest did not accept this explanation. Consequently, Laundry team retrieved the jacket for further inspection and informed the ADHSKP of the situation.

At 8:30 p.m., upon returning all laundered garments, including the Moncler down jacket, to the guestroom, ADHSKP personally visited the guest to offer an apology and ensure satisfaction. The guest confirmed that the smoke odor was no longer present. Regarding the scratches, ADHSKP explained that if any issue had occurred during the wash process, similar damage would likely have appeared on other areas of the jacket, however it was not in this case. The guest acknowledged this reasoning but expressed that the entire matter regarding the smoke smell had caused inconvenience and requested compensation.

To address the concern, ADHSKP offered to waive the laundry charge for the jacket. The guest remained dissatisfied, prompting the Duty Manager to be notified. DM contacted the guest directly to apologize, and guest shared the above incidents has caused her time and is a hassle. She shared that 1st the jacket returned have smell after wash, and HSKP did not offer anything until she had to voice out. DM showed understanding and offered to waive the entire laundry bill as a gesture of goodwill with guest's appreciation.

Photos showed below are before wash. (Could not indicate the areas guest said has scratches as one would need to pull open the inner area near zippers as the down feather is puffy. Laundry team inspected jacket before wash and did not notice scratches)
rows.Subject: 1905 | Ms. Min Tang | Laundry
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Guest sent laundry to wash on 26 Jan morning: 1 pair of jeans,  2 x dresses,  1 x jacket (Moncler)
Photos shown below are after wash,  with minor scratches near zippers around chest area.
The price of concerned jacket is around HK$15, 000.
DM will see off guest upon departure accordingly.

After guest has checked and confirmed all of their personal belongings in room were intact, they have requested from DM for room change due to feeling insecure in room. Guest reiterated about their negative experience during VDH breakfast about staff attitude issue which she would like to request for either room upgrade to suite or shorten stay to check out on 28 Jan instead of 30 Jan with room rate reduction. rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

-At 9:12hrs,  Ms Dong and her mother left Rm 2506 for VDH breakfast
-At 9:15hrs,  they arrived VDH and were greeted by Hostess in Mandarin. Since having no response from guest,  Hostess changed to speak with guest in English
-Only one Hostess was working at that time,  after guests provided room number to hostess,  they tried to enter the restaurant by themselves and they have been stopped by the hostess and being acknowledged to wait to be seated. Then,  a table in Gaddi's dining room has been arranged for them in around 30 sec.
-During breakfast,  guests have looked for section captain for paper napkin and chopstick which those are not a standard table setup for breakfast. 
-At around 9:50hrs,  Ms Dong (daughter) approached Steve to reflect her comment about staff attitude issue concerning hostess of VDH (unwelcoming in tone,  with smile,  and being impatient) and the impression of having insufficient staff working there. Case was referred to Kenneth
-At 9:56:09hrs,  guest and her mother returned to their room and attempted to open room door and found door security chain being activated
-At 9:56:39hrs,  guest approached a RA on same floor for assistance. Concern RA ask guest to wait which she will contact with someone to provide assistance.
-At 9:59hrs,  guest called Operator to report the situation and requested for assistance. Case was referred to DM
-At 10:03hrs,  DM met with guest in front of Rm 2506 and confirmed about the situation of door security chain being activated. Sincere apologies were extended about the inconvenience caused.
-At 10:04hrs,  Asst SOR Supervisor arrived the scene
-Ms Dong expressed her security concern about having someone entered their room without their authorization. DM checked with SOR and confirmed surveillance was reviewed and confirmed no one has entered their room after guest went for breakfast. Finding has been referred to guest.
-At 10:06:56hrs,  ENG technician arrived and to resolve the situation by uninstalling the security chain
-At 10:07:53hrs,  issue was resolved and guest successfully entered their room.  
-After guest entered the room,  DM has confirmed with guest that all of their personal belongings were intact.
-In between,  SOR has mentioned the security chain could have been accidentally triggered while guest left their room which guest was abit upset for such statement. Then,  DM assured guest that ENG Technician will inspect the condition of the security door chain.
-Guest then requested for room change since feeling insecure about staying in same room. 

-Duty ENG and DM have inspected the condition of door security chain lock which confirmed it functioned normally.

-At 7:30pm,  DOR called guest and to show concern about their experience. Guest highlighted the negative experience regarding the approach of Hostess in VDH. Also,  guest complimented the concern RA being helpful during their interaction and the attentive service from FDA during check-in,  which these feedback were being acknowledged. rows.Incident Description:
Ms. Elisa Chan joined the Star Ferry second session afternoon tea event. While walking in the waiting area, she unfortunately fell and said her right hand was numb. We immediately informed the Star Ferry company, who sent a dock controller to help her. They offered to take her to the hospital for a check-up, which she agreed to at first. However, just before the ferry was about to leave, she changed her mind and decided to board the ferry to continue with the event, mentioning that she would go to the hospital for treatment afterward. The ADFB and banquet manager were informed.

Action: The ADFB greeted Ms Chan as she got off the ferry and provided her business card. She had a great time and said she would go to the hospital for an examination with friend. The ADFB will make a follow up call to Ms Chan tomorrow.

Finding: The Star Ferry company did not put up the rain curtain during the rain, causing water to come into the waiting area and make the floor slippery. After we reminded them, they quickly sent staff to warn new guests to be careful of the slippery floor and placed two “Caution: Slippery Floor” signs in that area.

rows.Incident Description:
At 23:06 SOR conducted patrol and found a male outsider was sleeping in 8/F Pool male toilet. SOR approached the individual and informed him that sleeping was not allowed and asked him how he accessed The Pool. 
According to the male outsider, he followed other guests into the elevator to reach a guest floor, then used the stair to access the 8/F pool area and want to find a place to sleep. After the conversation, SOR escorted the male outsider out of the hotel.
rows.Subject: 08/F Others |     | Outsider Misbehaviour
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
According to CCTV footage:
At 21:35 the male outsider entered the Hotel via forecourt east main entrance.
At 21:35 the male outsider followed the couple of room #2105 entered guest lift#23. He tried to press the buttons of 5/F and 2/F but failed. Finally,  couple of room #2105 used the key card and pressed 27/F button.
At 21:36 couple of room #2105 and male outsider left the guest lift#23 on 27/F. Couple of room #2105 went to room #2716 side door,  and the male outsider went to outside room #2707.
At 21:37 couple of room #2105 had approached AHMR and the male outsider entered 27/F east BOH.
At 21:38 couple of room #2105 back to room #2105. Male outsider went to 30/F China Clipper back door and returned to ST3.
At 21:52 the male outsider arrived at 8/F and entered The Pool via back door next to service lift lobby.
At 21:59 the male outsider walked around The Pool and went into kitchen and collected some linen and went to the washroom.
At 23:05 SOR patrolled and found the male outsider was sleeping in the washroom.
At 23:06 SOR escorted the male outsider to leave the Hotel via service lift to G/F.
SOR checked the Kantech door of 27/F east several times and confirmed the door was in order. SOR found the back door and kitchen door were unlocked when he arrived and he had locked it afterwards. DE was informed and will remind ENG staff to lock the door when they finish the work daily.

rows.Incident Description: At 5:30pm, guest approached FD and yelling at the counter. AFOM approached the guest to offer assistance. According to the guest, he has been standing outside his room for 40minutes to wait for his room key since he claimed he was told that we shall send him the room key. At the same time, he was kept looking for the staff who approached him in the room earlier for confrontation. AFOM excused that the concerned staff was off duty already and was assured to look into the matter which the guest mentioned would look for AFOM again at 6:30pm for the investigation outcome.
rows.Subject: 2507 | Mr. Zhi Xiong Deng | Guest Comment
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 6:30pm,  guest returned to FD and looked for AFOM. Sales Mgr and AFOM met the guest,  explained the findings and the misunderstanding in between. However,  the guest claimed it was not the whole story of it and requested to check once again. He claimed he shall look for us again upon departure for a satisfactory outcome.

Findings:
- According to SFDA,  he went up to the room in order to collect the payment for the extension booking. However,  when he went up,  the guest told him that the payment would be made by his assistant. At the same time,  guest also requested for the room key which SFDA informed him that he need to double check but did not commit would make the room key at that moment. SFDA informed Sales Mgr about such which he agreed that we could only renew the room key after receiving the payment for the extension. Sales Mgr also assisted to communicate with the assistant with acknowledgement received.
- CCTV was reviewed,  SFDA met the guest at 5:05pm and left the scene at 5:07pm.
- At 5:16pm,  guest went out to the corridor and went down to lobby at 5:26pm.
- According to FDS,  the guest approached him and asked for the room key. FDS explained to him that payment is required for the extension room key,  and the guest claimed he has informed us the assistant would handle it,  and he was waiting at the corridor for the room key since he was told would be send to him. However,  neither FDS or SFDA noticed he went out of his room.
- Entire stay 30 Jan - 5 Feb

AFOM tried to convince the guest continue their stay however they insisted to leave tomorrow and demanded the full refund on the night on next day. Since they would like to take a rest, guest requested the outcome for their demand between 8-9am on next day.

rows.Incident Description:
Felix was fully privatized for a cocktail reception.
At 6:30 PM, guests began arriving, and the volume went over the expectations of the organizer. With the organizer’s approval, we continued welcoming guests as they arrived.
At around 8:45 PM, the organizer decided to stop admitting additional guests. Around 20 guests were queuing at the Felix lift lobby at that time. The event host went down to explain that the event had concluded and no more guests would be admitted. All waiting guests left by 9:20 PM.
Guests inside the restaurant continued to enjoy the event until 10:45 PM, all remaining guests departed smoothly.
Findings
The organizer expected 120 guests for the event.
The kitchen and service teams had already prepared extra food and beverages based on the expected headcount. At the end we did 150 pax for full menu guest and extra 80 pax for drinks.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Findings
Upon review,  it was determined that the hostess was missed to reach the guest for reconfirmation calls made the previous day. Due to this oversight,  the guest did not receive the information regarding the road closures,  which directly led to the incident.
  
Action:
The hostess team has been briefed on the requirement to strictly follow the Double-Call Procedure.
If the first confirmation call is unanswered,  staff must make a second attempt within two hours at a different time of the day. All call attempts and outcomes must be properly recorded in the reservation log.

A guests came for dinner for 2 pax this evening. The female guest required a gluten-free diet. The guests wished to order the pan‑fried beef fillet. However, Chef informed us that the beef had already been marinated with ingredients containing gluten, making it unsuitable for her dietary needs.
Upon learning this, the guest expressed disappointment. As gesture, we upgraded the beef fillet to Wagyu beef and provided a complimentary fruit platter in recognition of their anniversary celebration. The guests appreciated the follow‑up and left happily.

Prior to arrival,  the guests had used PenChat to pre‑order a gluten‑free version of the pan‑fried beef fillet. Unfortunately,  the teammate handling the request missing issue an official kitchen order resulting in the dietary requirement not being communicated to the kitchen team in advance.
  
Action Taken
-Reinforce staff awareness regarding allergen management and the importance of accurate communication through refresher training.
-Ensure all PenChat or pre‑arrival requests are promptly entered as official kitchen orders and verified before service.

rows.Incident Description:
Received an email regarding a guest's feedback about their dinner experience at The Lobby yesterday, 25th February.
 
Incident Details:
The guest ordered tea and specifically requested that it be served with dessert after the set menu. However, the tea was served immediately. The guest then informed a captain and asked for fresh tea to be served later with dessert. When dessert arrived, the guest believed the same pot of tea was brought back—it tasted fermented, stale, and overly strong. The guest observed a server pour out the old tea, add only hot water, and send it back. The guest commented that this shortcut was unhygienic, unsafe, and unprofessional. For a luxury hotel, such behaviour is unacceptable. Reusing tea leaves misleads guests and shows disrespect.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

RM spoke with guest by phone this afternoon. We offered our sincere apologies and informed him that staff training will be enhanced to reinforce professional service standards. He is a regular guest,  visiting every two to three months. He did not request compensation but provided feedback to ensure this does not happen again.
 
Action Taken:
We will brief the team thoroughly and provide training to uphold professional service standards.

rows.Incident Description:
A guest enjoyed dinner at Felix. While settling the bill, the payment terminal prompted for the credit card password. The guest stated he had never used a password for his card and did not have another credit card or cash available.
The Restaurant Manager approached the table and explained that overseas transactions may require additional verification. The RM proposed processing the payment in smaller amounts, which the guest agreed. The charges were successfully completed in three separate transactions.
After departing the restaurant, the guest went to FO. He expressed appreciation for the team’s assistance in finding a solution. However, he also shared that he felt uncomfortable, as he believed the RM’s explanation may not have been delivered discreetly enough. He suspected that the next table was aware of the situation, which caused embarrassment.

Finding
The guest was seated at Table 51, located next to the speaker. During the DJ performance, the volume was elevated. The RM leaned in and bent over to communicate and offer solutions due to the noise level, which may have contributed to the guest’s perception of insufficient discretion.

Action
ADFNBO was informed of the case and attempted a courtesy call to the guest, but was unable to reach him. VM left and will continue the follow-up.
rows.Subject: Felix Restaurant | Mr. Frank  Coroon | Guest Comment - F&B
rows.Investigation Remarks 1: ADFB finally reached the guest who appreciated the genuine follow up and explanation provided. Personal contact details shared for next visit in PHK or other sister properties.

rows.Incident Description:
A guest with two sons arrived and wished to queue for afternoon tea. At 2pm, our non-Chinese speaking hostess was greeting guests in the queue and explaining the afternoon tea details one by one. When the hostess approached the fourth party, the guest became very agitated and requested Chinese-speaking assistance. The non-Chinese speaking hostess returned to the reception desk to ask another hostess for help, then proceeded to the fifth party to continue greeting.
However, after the Chinese-speaking hostess explained the situation and went back to the reception desk, the lady from the fourth party pointed at the non-Chinese speaking hostess again and shouted at her using inappropriate language. A captain noticed the situation and replaced the non-Chinese speaking hostess. Another hostess then seated the party immediately. The non-Chinese speaking hostess reported the incident to AFNB.
AFNB approached the table and explained to the guest that her behaviour had made our staff feel uncomfortable. She had shouted at the hostess using inappropriate English words, though she continued speaking in Chinese. Her son showed understanding and extended an apology on her behalf.
rows.Subject: The Lobby Restaurant | N/A N/A | Guest Misbehaviour
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Findings:
A guest approached the reception desk at 1pm to enquire about afternoon tea. At that time,  the queue had not yet formed,  and no one was waiting,  so she left. Around 1:45pm,  when the non-Chinese speaking hostess noticed the guest standing near the reception desk and wishing to have afternoon tea,  she escorted her to the queue. By then,  three parties were already waiting. However,  the guest claimed she had arrived at 1pm and should have been first in line. She alleged that the non-Chinese speaking hostess had caused her to wait longer.
Action:
Clearly communicate the queue area and queuing time to guests in advance to prevent any misunderstandings or dissatisfaction.

rows.Incident Description:
Guest sent an email to GMO regarding the staying experience, comments as below: 
1.Multiple attempts needed to get a response from the hotel regarding the reservation. 
2.Guest was not able to modify his reservation on Peninsula website
3.Inconsistent communication led to repeated questions on arrival details. Then, they were being approached one day prior the arrival to inquire about such details.
4.Last-minute car service request was declined; response was brief and unhelpful. 
5.Hotel has not checked with guest prior to arrival about bedding preference which twin room was assigned but they prefer a room with King bed.
6.Service delay on delivering a bucket of ice. 
7.Shower's mechanism was worn, causing inconsistent operation between handheld and overhead options.
rows.Subject: 444 | Mr. Ben Tyson | Guest Comment
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Findings:
Point 1: 
-On 2 Nov 25,  the initial guest inquiry was sent,  response was sent the same day,  but it was an automated response requesting the property name
-On 3 Nov 25,  guest replied,  and GCSC agent responded the same day,  reassuring that the booking was in order
Point 2:
-On 1 Nov 25,  an email was received from Cathay Holidays for guest's booking of a Deluxe room. No bedding type was specified.
-On 2 Nov 25,  guest sent email to GCSC,  mentioning he booked via Cathay Holidays but could not locate the booking on the Peninsula portal. An auto-reply was sent to the guest on the same day asking which property he had reserved. Guest replied "PHK, " on 3 Nov 2025. On the same day,  GCSC replied that his booking was in good order.
-On 5 Jan 26,  his wife sent email to the general PHK mailbox and stated that she could not locate the booking online. She sent another email on 6 Jan 26 as she has not received a reply. On the same day,  GCSC confirmed her booking was in good order.
-On 8 Jan 26,  his wife wrote another email to provide flight information. It was acknowledged by GCSC with no additional services or assistance being offered.
-On 5 Feb 26,  his wife inquired about the cost of an airport transfer. GCSC provided a quote,  but she has not replied to that email.
Point 3:
-On 2 Mar 26,  a standard pre-arrival email was sent to guest by GCSC.
-On 6 Mar 26,  guest asked for an upgrade. Request was responded by GCSC at 20:53 on 7 Mar 26 (same day of guest's arrival) which it will be subjected to hotel availability.
Point 4:
-At 12:06 on 7 Mar,  guest sent an email to GCSC to request for airport transfer. At 16:29,  GCSC replied that no cars was available. Alternative (Airport Express and taxi) were being introduced to guest which they replied "thank you."
-On 7 Mar,  all 4 drivers on duty were assigned with transfer order,  including one on-hire. B&T offered GCSC to check the availability of outsourced car company but GCSC has not made any reply. GCSC mentioned that they got the message that no car was available including outsource service.
Point 5:
-Booking was set up as a Deluxe Twin Room by GCSC with no bedding preference specified. Room upgrade request was added on the booking preference by GCSC at 20:51 on 7 Mar but communication has not been made to FD,  including Shiji note.
-Upon check-in,  guest was initially assigned a Deluxe Room with twin beds (# 543). Learn that guest would like to have a solid king bed,  guest was then assigned to a Deluxe King(#444). Due to noise concern about AiR canopy work,  Deluxe Courtyard Room was not assigned.
Point 6:
-Guest request the bucket of ice through B&T and hotSOS order was issued by PABX.
-RA has delivered the ice bucket to 4/F but failed to send to room since guest was not there. RA has verified with Operator and was advised to put on hold on the delivery and to wait for guest's return.
Point 7:
-According to DoE,  the pull button was working properly,  and the issue was caused by shower head hose leaking,  which replacement was made.

Alice Lai (11 Mar 2026)
At 11:18am,  guest sent PenChat and requested to have someone look into the shower as guest was having trouble keeping the water to come out of wall head only. When guest pull the lever out it stays out some of the time but not all of the time which is quite frustrating.
AFOM,  Asst HSKP Mgr and ENG attended to the room and confirmed all functions in shower cubicle are working properly. 
Guest was invited to meet up in person for more understanding via PenChat,  awaiting to reply.

Glenn Bautista (13 Mar 2026)
At 07:38 Guest replied PenChat and requested a demonstration on how to operate the shower.
Night Manager proceeded to the room and showed sharer Ms Burton,  Lucie how to use the shower "pull knob" water diverter and other water spray options of the shower head which was appreciated.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
A RM approached the guest and offered an apology. The guest responded positively and ultimately enjoyed their breakfast. He departed at 10:00 AM without any further comments or concerns.

Log Update - 14 March
Today,  Mr. Kim from Room 313 arrived at Verandah for breakfast at 09:30. At that time,  the restaurant was experiencing a peak period with approximately 100 guests within the hour,  resulting in a queue for seating. Subsequently,  the guest decided to have breakfast at the Lobby instead.

Action Taken:
A breakfast buffet table at Verandah has been reserved for the guest until check-out on 16 March

Finding: The Verandah Café was closed so reduced seating capacity due to the setup of an art piece.
 
Action: Gaddis will set up the breakfast for a backup.

rows.Incident Description:
Mr Zeiss from Room 2111 visited for breakfast today and shared feedback regarding his dining experience yesterday. At the same time, we also received an email comment regarding this case.He mentioned that the steak served yesterday was not hot enough, so he asked for it to be heated. However, the chef only reheated the same piece of steak he had taken instead of preparing a new one. The guest felt that this was unhygienic and unprofessional.

Manager immediately apologized again for the unsatisfactory dining experience and provided his business card to the guest should he need any further assistance in the future.

Finding:
At the time, the chef misunderstood the guest’s request. As the chef was not aware that the guest expected a new steak to be prepared, he simply reheated the steak that the guest had already taken.

Action:
This incident will be addressed with the kitchen team. Additional training will be conducted to ensure staff listen carefully to guests’ requests and clearly understand their needs. Team members will also be reminded to take extra care of guest expectations and handle such requests appropriately to prevent similar situations from happening again.

rows.Incident Description:
At 6:15am, after the guest had checked out and was waiting for her Uber transfer to the airport, the guest approached the Duty Manager to question the room rate applied to her booking, stating that it differed from the rate confirmed by GCSC.
The rate being applied to guest’s booking under Grand Deluxe Room:
HK$6500+13% for (14 and 15 Mar); Complimentary night on 16 Mar (Total HK$14690)
Guest showed the email communication with GCSC on 29 Jan which she got the rate quote for staying period (14 - 17 Mar) stating - Room rate: HK$4334 per room per night under “More Time … With Our Compliments” offer (Third night free). Guest subsequently sent email to GCSC on 2 Feb to confirm the booking. 
DM addressed her concern and explained the rate mechanism of the package. A booking confirmation email outlining the room rate details was sent to the guest on 3 Feb, and the rate stated therein matched the rate applied to the guest’s booking. Unfortunately, the guest did not accept the explanation and stated that the hotel was “lying” to her.
As the guest was in a hurry to catch her airport transfer, she requested the hotel to review the situation and provide a response by email after her departure.

-On same day,  GCSC replied guest with the room type option with rate quote,  which the rate quote of Grand Deluxe room was stating: Room rate: HK$4334 per room per night under “More Time … With Our Compliments” offer (Third night free).
-On 2 Feb,  guest sent email to GCSC to confirm the booking.
-On 3 Feb,  GCSC sent an email confirmation with rate details stating: HK$6500+13% for (14 and 15 Mar); Complimentary night on 16 Mar.
-AFDM assisted guest for check-in which guest has signed the Registration form with rate details stating on it. Guest has not brought up her concern about rate variance.
-Guest has encountered ESD issue during stay regarding 2 spotlights next to window could not be shut at night time,  case was logged under Incident Number IC-02391-001.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

-Guest requested to put on waitlist and was asked for the telephone number,  which guest provided but questioned why Operator requested her number if it has been showed on the display,  Operator then replied as normal procedure.
-Operator then searched her number in system but wrongly addressed as Ms Liu,  which guest showed her disappointment and requested to speak with the manager after she engaged with another call.
-Telephone Services Manager subsequently extended follow up call to guest,  however she wrongly addressed her name as Ms Lau and Ms Wong respectively. 
-Guest repeated her dissatisfaction of the hotel service and the handling,  requested the email and name of GM.
-At the end,  guest was informed that the situation was reviewed and able to arrange for her accordingly. Guest requested email as confirmation which Lobby team was informed to follow up.
-At around 7:30pm,  AFOM tried to reach out to guest mobile but no answer. Voice mail was left with invitation for a follow up call.
Finding:
-It was reviewed that there was a previous patron called Ms Liu with her phone Chinese mobile number including part of Ms Lee's number,  thus Operator mistakenly addressed guest as Ms Liu. 
-For addressing guest as Ms Wong,  Operator wrongly heard that the guest mentioned her name as Ms Wong.

She comment we should verify the number from our side instead of having the guest speaking out the number on the street or somewhere that is not convenient for them. AFOM showed understanding on the situation and was assured corrective training shall be conducted. She claimed she have drafted the email to hotel management and would send it out soon. rows.Incident Description: At 18:20, a party of 2 persons arrived for dinner. Their food order was placed at 18:40. One of the ordered dishes, “Stewed Beef Brisket with Chinese Celery in Beef Broth,” was served after 50 minutes, exceeding the expected service time and resulting in guest dissatisfaction.
rows.Subject: Spring Moon | Ms. Qing Sheng | 1 Incident Case
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The Manager approached the guests promptly to offer sincere apologies for the delay. As a gesture of goodwill,  a complimentary dessert was offered. However,  the guests declined as they were already full. Subsequently,  a complimentary box of walnuts was presented as an alternative gesture,  which the guests accepted and appreciated.
 
Findings:
	1.	Total dinner covers at the time: 184 pax
	2.	The Section‑in‑Charge confirmed that the kitchen was not informed in a timely manner,  leading to the service delay.
 
Action plan:
	1.	Service staff to actively monitor dish preparation times and follow up with the kitchen if any dish exceeds the standard service time.
	2.	Provide refresher training for service staff on effective communication,  order recall,  and timely escalation to supervisors when delays are identified.

rows.Incident Description: At 3:40pm, guest called to hotel by her mobile to reconfirm her Star Ferry afternoon tea booking, she was told the afternoon tea booked at The Lobby instead, which guest showed huge disappointment of the wrong venue booked. Guest reluctantly accepted the afternoon tea at The Lobby at 4pm and requested to meet up with manager.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
At 4pm,  AFOM approached and learned that guest requested Star Ferry afternoon tea upon arrival,  which staff booked table for 3 at 3:30pm at The Lobby. Guest later approached staff at lobby,  asked how to get to the ferry pier as her booking at 3pm,  staff reminded her to be there by 2:45pm with the route to ferry pier,  but without telling her that there was no slot under 3pm. Guest waited for long time at the ferry pier and was toldby staff there later that the next slot at 4pm instead. Guest then called back to hotel and verified.
Later when guest entered to room,  she found that the bedding type was incorrect,  it should be King bed instead of twin bed. Bedding was changed to King accordingly.
Sincere apologies extended for both unpleasant experience and guest was assured that investigation will be taken. As token of apology,  DRR and amenities arranged with guest appreciated.
Finding:
-Checked with FDA who claimed that guest did not mention star ferry but afternoon tea only.
-Check with concerned staff who stationed at The Lobby,  who did not realize the star ferry time slot. 
-According to RO,  guest requested King bed,  but GCSC wrongly input as twin bed.

rows.Incident Description: At 3:30pm, Mr Liu and his friends approached Concierge to file a complaint regarding the cancelled helicopter ride.
rows.Subject: Outlet Patron | Yu Feng Liu | Guest Comment - F&B
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
As learnt,  Mr Liu received weather call at 1:30pm that the flight might not be able to fly due to visibility and final weather call will be extended at 2:30pm,  which was confirmed not able to fly after.
Subsequently,  friend of Mr Liu requested access to helipad for photo shooting only,  however,  was quoted additional price without concerning their situation. 
AFOM approached and arranged helipad photo session at once with their appreciated. Friend of Mr Liu commented hotel should notice the weather was not good in the morning and should inform them prior their lunch at 1pm,  instead of 2:30pm,  which affected their proposal plan. Also,  staff could have been more flexible on arranging photo session. They appreciated the arrangement at the end and requested a follow up with Mr Liu for the cancellation. 
AFOM tried to call after liaised with F&B management but no answer. Voice mail has been left and email was sent.
Finding:
-Guest booked Fly and Dine package for six,  lunch at 1pm at SPM and flight at 3:30pm.
-Flight delay or cancellation subjected to weather condition have been indicated on the confirmation email. 
-Checked with Heli Services,  the flight of 11:30am has been cancelled which informed F&B team,  thus guest was contacted about this situation at 1:30pm,  and final weather call was conducted at 2:30pm with Mr Liu acknowledged.
-Weather call usually conduct one hour in advance as normal practice.

rows.Incident Description:
At 5:00 PM on 26 March, Hotel Guest (2412) Ms. Yuen Wing Chee received a treatment. The next day after the treatment, on 27 March, the guest call GR and wanted to talk to the Spa Manager. Guest then approached our Spa Director and commented on her treatment. The guest experienced pain in her left arm and noticed bruising after the treatment. She informed the Spa Director that she did not raise her concerns with the therapist as guest thought that therapist would see her scar on her left arm and either avoid the scar area or be soft over that area. She did not mention the wound on her left arm, as the dark scar was already visible to the therapist. However, the therapist applied strong pressure, which caused pain and redness in the affected area.
The Spa Director apologized for the incident and offered to apply soothing oil to help ease and reduce the redness. First aid was also offered. However, the guest declined as she did not wish to escalate the issue. The guest expressed that she only wanted to inform us of the issue to help prevent a similar incident from happening again.
As a gesture of goodwill, she was offered a pouch of VOYA products. Before she left, the guest mentioned that the massage for her husband received was satisfying and good. Spa Director provided her contact information should the guest experience any discomfort.
rows.Subject: Group Of Guest | Treatment Issue
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
The Spa Director has checked with the therapist and confirmed that the guest did not raise any comments or concerns before or during the treatment. The therapist followed standard consultation procedures by asking the guest if there were any areas to focus on or avoid. During the treatment,  the therapist also checked with the guest regarding pressure,  and the guest confirmed that it was comfortable.
Following this matter,  the Spa Director has briefed all therapists to remain vigilant in observing any wounds,  scars,  or sensitive areas on the guest’s body. Therapists are reminded to consult with guests before massaging such areas to ensure comfort and safety.

AFNB contacted the guest to provide an explanation. Guest understood the situation and expressed willingness to return in the future.

Findings:
As we are currently running an art event, the cake selection is intentionally curated to align with the artistic theme. Due to the café being fully occupied at the time, the team was unable to explain the concept and connection between the cakes and the art pieces to the guest. Regarding the charging issue, the existing charging cables do not support fast charging, which resulted in slower charging speed for the guest’s device.

Action:
Team will be briefed to proactively explain the art concept behind the cake selection to enhance guest understanding and experience. And the team will review and improve the charging facilities, including providing faster charging options where possible.

Assistant Manager sincerely apologized to the guest and explained that additional preparation time was required to ensure food safety due to the allergy concern. Guest understood the explanation and left without further comments.

- Guest ordered Caesar Salad with chicken and no bacon, grilled panini without mortadella
- During 4pm, there were 3 orders from Verandah Cafe and 2 orders from private dining and 1 order from pool.

Action:
The team will ensure clearer communication of waiting time, especially for special dietary or allergy-related orders. And kitchen team will be notified in advance to prioritize such orders where possible to minimize waiting time.

rows.Incident Description:
The booking was made through Senior Captain on 4 March. She assisted the guest with pre-ordering the dishes, including two whole suckling pigs,on 26 March.

At around 7:10 pm, Amuse bouche and the appetizer trio was served . The guest claimed that the suckling pig was expected to be served as the first course instead. When the suckling pigs were ready to be served, the guest felt that two whole suckling pigs were excessive and requested to cancel one order .

The Manager  promptly approached the guest and extended sincere apologies the oversight. The guest appreciated the follow up for cancel the  whole suckling pig. Subsequently, the Senior Captain also approached the guest to apologize again for the mistake, which the guest accepted with understanding.

Finding: 
The Senior Captain had knowledge that the sucking pig requires around 20 minutes of preparation, while the appetizer has a shorter preparation time. This information was not communicated to the guest during the pre order process.

Action : 
The service team will be reminded and retrained during daily morning briefings and after lunch operations today to ensure clear communication with guests.
Orders and serving sequences must be reconfirmed clearly, especially for pre-ordered dishes and set menus.
Upon guest arrival, the team must reconfirm all pre-orders and the intended serving sequence to prevent similar incidents from recurring.

At 21:15, Mr. Alexander Nestle’s group arrived after dining at Chesa. 
Mr. Nestle thought the front room had been reserved for his group and surprisingly saw that a couple remained seated at the bar counter. 

The head mixologist explained to Mr. Nestle that the venue only offers full-venue privatization. As an alternative, we offered a table adjacent to the piano and the bar counter area.

rows.Incident Description:
At 8:50am, guest sent email to FD and comment the followings:
1) No booking was found upon arrival and took an hour to settle down
2) Room key was not functioning on 31 Mar
3) Requested late check out but being informed additional charge shall occurred
4) Guest informed by TA that someone from hotel would contact them regarding the reservation but did not receive any call
rows.Subject: 2109 | Mr. Ian Courtney Perryman | Guest Comment
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
DoFO called to room and extended apologies. Late check out as well as one round of drink at The Lobby prior leaving the hotel was offered with guest acceptance.
At 4:30pm,  DoFO greeted the guest upon departure. Guest appreciated with the assistance without further complication. Follow up email has been sent to guest by DoFO.

Findings:
- At 6:30pm on 29 Mar,  guest approached FD for check in. However,  the booking was cancelled and no new booking was found at that moment. Since it took time to clarify the reservation,  FDA offered hotel BAR rate for 1 night to guest while checking with GCSC and TA with guest acceptance. Guest completed the check in process at 7:15pm and was escorted to room. Guest was assured would provide update to them once the issue was sorted out.
- According to GCSC,  booking was made on 20 Jun 2025 under CGK with external reference number UA191R -PPTD87. However,  they received amendment request from TA on 25 Jun that guest would like to reserve CS2 instead,  however,  the booking was not able to amend in TA system. Therefore,  GCSC manually amended the booking in system under the same hotel confirmation number but a new external reference number (UA191R) was given as requested.
- On 26 Jul,  GCSC received the cancellation request under external reference number UA191R-PPTD87,  however,  the concerned GCSC staff was not aware about the new external reference number under the same hotel confirmation number,  therefore the booking was cancelled.
- At 7:41pm,  the booking issue was rectified. FDS did contact the guest about the update,  however,  it was failed to remind guest to update the room key which caused the key malfunctioned on 31 Mar.
- Regarding the late check out,  TA called GCSC on 31 Mar and asked for late check out,  due to availability,  late check out 12:30pm was offered.

rows.Incident Description:
On 24 Mar at 3:30 am, a complaint from the wedding couple, Ms. Janice Chu & Mr. Alan Sze, who hosted a wedding lunch on 21 March 2026, was received. The email outlined 12 points of concerns. During a wedding event, multiple service and coordination issues were reported, including insufficient room setup in the Chinese Nuptial package (Deluxe Suite and Superior Courtyard Suite) to support for the tea ceremony, limited on-site event assistance and gaps in communication when guests arrived before venue readiness. Delays between banquet courses, video cue errors, and food quality concerns were also raised. Additionally, the seating plan was not co-ordinated as expected, resulting in guest confusion. Overall, the incident highlighted coordination, service attentiveness and proactiveness, and execution gaps across banquet service, food service and event planning.

Findings:
DOE contacted the guest on 25 and 27 March. Mr. Sze did not agree with several points based on our findings. An apology letter, acknowledging service and coordination gaps, was sent to the guest on 30 March and outlined our remedial actions and sincere apologies.

To enhance the guest’s upcoming stay on 11–12 April, we offered a complimentary upgrade from Deluxe HV Room to Deluxe HV Suite and a dining credit.

Bar Log – 3 April 2026

IHG#615
Mr. Panday arrived at the bar with his family at 11:30pm. We courteously explained the dress code and children policy. He then arranged for Mrs. Modi and the three children to return to the room, while he remained with us. Mr. Panday enjoyed three rounds of drinks and departed at 1:20am.

Finding:
Guest expectations regarding late‑night bar access and children policy highlight the need for clearer, consistent communication across all teams.

rows.Incident Description:
Received an email regarding a guest's comment about the afternoon tea service.
 
First of all, when the guest raised his hand to request a refill of hot water, the server misunderstood and presented the bill to him. The guest explained that they were not finished yet, but the server insisted that his gesture was a request for the check, rather than apologizing for the mix-up, and appeared annoyed.
 
The guest claimed the service was unprofessional. As the guest mentioned to the server that they had not yet finished the afternoon tea and the scone was still on the stand, the server continued to take away the three-tier stand and replied to the guest, "Taking the stand away and giving the scone back to you, is that okay?" He then placed the plate with the scone back on the table with a poker face. The guest felt this was a very rude demeanor.
rows.Subject: The Lobby Restaurant | Chris Mok | Guest Comment - F&B
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Finding:
When the guest raised his hand,  the server was aware but was collecting plates from the next table. He did not approach the guest to confirm what he actually needed and made an explanation that was inappropriate and not in line with service manners. Later,  when the server believed the meal was almost finished,  he attempted to provide turndown service and wanted to clear the afternoon tea stand. However,  he took the afternoon tea stand from the table without asking for permission. The guests stated they were not finished,  yet he over-explained,  and the guests felt it was odd.
 
Action:
AFNB was called to speak with the guest and extended a sincere apology. The guest understood and did not require any further assistance.
 
The team will be properly briefed on correct communication with guests.

rows.Incident Description:
A total of 5 in-house guests participated in the Dim Sum Cooking Class from 10:00 am to 12:00 pm, followed by lunch service at Spring Moon. It was noted in advance that one guest has a shellfish allergy, and this information was communicated to the kitchen team during the pre‑order process.

During lunch service, when the dish “Stewed noodles with marinated sliced pork, spring onions, and Sichuan spicy sauce” was served, the guest raised a concern regarding a powder-like garnish on the noodles after tasting the dish. The service team immediately verified the ingredient with the chef, who confirmed that shrimp roe had been added as a garnish.

The server promptly informed the guest that the garnish contained shrimp roe and advised that it should not be consumed due to the allergy. The dish was immediately replaced with a new portion without shrimp roe.

The manager in charge promptly approached the guest to express concern and offer sincere apologies. A business card was provided to the guest for any further assistance if required.
The guests appreciated the prompt follow-up and handling of the situation. No allergic reaction occurred.
 
Findings
 
The kitchen order clearly indicated the shellfish allergy, and instructions were given to modify dishes accordingly.
The kitchen assistant admitted to overlooking the special order and added shrimp roe out of habit.
 
 
Action Taken
 
-The Chef in Charge will review food preparation procedures with the kitchen team.
-Additional training will be conducted to reinforce strict compliance with allergy-related orders.
rows.Subject: Spring Moon | Ms. Monique Devlin | 1 Incident Case

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
After inspection,  staff informed the guest that the attachment was firmly secured and that removing it might cause damage to the pants. With the guest’s consent,  staff proceeded to carefully remove the pants from the hook. During the removal process,  noticeable damage to the pants occurred.
RM approached the table promptly to address the situation and extended sincere apologies to the guest. As a gesture of goodwill,  two glasses of champagne were offered,  and the first round of drinks was waived.
The guest acknowledged that the incident was an isolated case and expressed appreciation for the prompt follow-up and service recovery. The guest also mentioned intentions to return in the coming days. Contact were exchanged to assist with future reservations.

Findings: Long Table attached with hook-and-loop tape for table skirt use for different event. Guest was wearing a silk and lace pants,  while guest seating down accidently attached her pants on it.
 
Action: Review with HSPK to apply material to cover the hook to avoid similar case happen.

rows.Incident Description:
At 13:40, a phone call was received from a Front Office colleague reporting that a hotel guest had shared feedback regarding their lunch experience yesterday(9/April), stating that both food quality and service did not meet expectations.
At 15:40, as the guests were departing the hotel, the Manager and the F&B in charge approached them to offer sincere apologies. As a gesture of goodwill, two sets of walnut sauce and XO sauce were presented to the guests. The guests expressed thanks and appreciation for the prompt follow-up.
 
Findings
 
	1.	The guests ordered stir-fried baby spinach. After the dish was served, the guests commented that it was tasteless and appeared to be poached rather than stir‑fried.
The server immediately apologized and offered to replace the dish using an alternative cooking method.
The guest requested that the dish be retained in stir-fried style. A replacement dish was promptly prepared and served accordingly.
After serving the replacement, the assistant manager checked on the guest’s satisfaction, and the guest confirmed that the dish was satisfactory.
However, today the guest expressed dissatisfaction that the satisfaction check was conducted in front of his accompanying guest, which he perceived as uncomfortable.
 
 
	2.	When the guest requested order egg tarts, they were informed that 15-minute preparation time was required. Due to the waiting time, the guest decided not to proceed with the order.
 
 
Action Taken
 
	1.	Conduct refresher training for service staff on attentive table observation and timely engagement, ensuring guest comfort is maintained at all times.
	2.	Reinforce appropriate timing and discretion when checking guest satisfaction, particularly when guests are dining with companions.

rows.Incident Description: At around 5:30 PM, external guest Ms. Kat Lei approached the reception and shared her disappointment. She mentioned that her therapist’s nails were long and felt scratchy during the massage on her lower back. She also stated that the temperature was too hot. However, the therapist addressed the issue immediately by turning off the heat pad. She also mentioned the pressure applied on her back might have caused her to experience lower back pain, but it was manageable.
rows.Subject: Outside Guest | Kat Lei | Treatment Issue
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
We asked if she would like to speak with our Spa Director,  but the guest declined. She commented that overall,  the experience was unsatisfactory. Spa receptions apologized for the uncomfortable experience,  and as a gesture,  we offered her a gift. We also asked if she would like a manager to call her back. She preferred that we send an email to Mr. Johan Gjengstone (johan@cta.no).
Mr. Johan Gjengstone commented that his experience was good.
1.	The therapist consulted the guest prior to the treatment,  and no concerns were raised at that time. During the treatment,  the therapist regularly checked with the guest to ensure the pressure was acceptable.
2.	Upon receiving the guest’s comment about the therapist’s nails during the treatment,  the therapist apologized and showed her nails to the guest. The apology was acknowledged. The therapist did not observe any resistance or discomfort from the guest when applying pressure thereafter.
3.	The therapist did not see any scratch marks during or after the treatment.
4.	The therapist focused on the lower back for 45 minutes,  as per the guest’s request.
5.	The Spa Director checked the therapist’s nails and find out it is short and could not be shorter.

rows.Investigation Remarks 1:

While the Chef initially confirmed the dish did not contain nuts,  a subsequent review with the entire Chinese culinary team revealed that nuts were indeed an ingredient. While clearing the main course,  guest mentioned the chicken was too dry. RM brought the chicken back to chef for verification – Cooking temperature and texture appeared to be satisfactory.

rows.Incident Description:
Room guest Ms Cao (Room 2203) visited The Verandah for breakfast with her family (4 pax). During the service, the guest raised a comment regarding the chef’s attitude at the egg station.
Upon being informed, Manager immediately approached the guest, offered a sincere apology, and attempted to follow up by arranging a replacement order. However, the guest clarified that she only wished to share feedback and did not require further action.
Case was informed to SESC & EAM.
rows.Subject: Verandah | Mr. Pei Cao | Guest Comment - F&B
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Findings:
The guest initially requested one portion of over-easy eggs,  and the chef informed her that it would take a few minutes. When the guest returned the second time,  the dish was not yet ready,  and she did not check with the chef before leaving. As the guest did not return for some time,  the chef assumed the order was no longer required and served a similar item to another guest. When the guest returned for the third time and enquired about the order,  the chef immediately prepared a new portion. The guest felt that the chef had forgotten her order.

Action:
A briefing will be conducted with the culinary team to reinforce that:
Clear and polite communication on waiting time must be provided to guests.
Orders should be reconfirmed and properly tracked until completion.
Proactive follow-up is required to avoid any misunderstanding or perception of neglect.

Assistant Manager immediately approached the guest with a sincere apology and enquired about his needs. The guest mentioned that he was only providing feedback and hoped for improvement. He acknowledged that it appeared to be an isolated case and did not raise any further comments upon departure.

This case has been reported to the EAM and ESC.
rows.Subject: Verandah | Georgy  Mikhaylets | Guest Comment - F&B
rows.Investigation Remarks 1:
Finding:
Guest placed an order at the egg station for three eggs with mushrooms and tomatoes,  fried and well done. At the same time,  there were two other similar orders also requesting three eggs,  which led to a misunderstanding by the chef,  who initially prepared scrambled eggs instead.
As the correct order required well-done fried eggs,  which take a longer preparation time,  the first delivery was incorrect. A new order had to be prepared,  resulting in a total waiting time of approximately 15–20 minutes.

Action:
As the guest will be checking out on 27 April,  we will arrange a table closer to the buffet area prior to his departure and assign a team member to assist with order-taking,  in order to prevent a recurrence of similar issues and enhance the guest experience.
